answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake, like a pearl held in escrow, before it may trade: creating thousands of fake agents then costs real capital per identity, and misbehavior burns the stake. Reputation grows slowly along a trellis of verified completed work, so a fresh marble-smooth new identity cannot outbid an established one. An attacker must pay the stake for every fake and wait out the slow reputation climb, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
